<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917894_theRebbe_634" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917894_theRebbe_634__p008">
  <section v="21">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on the above, the Zohar's phrase "I will show him" refers to Moshe, who opened the channel for future wonders during the Exodus, though it was hidden from him.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">2)</t>
    <t s="2">And based on all the above, we can explain what is said in the Zohar,</t>
    <t s="3">"I will show him"</t>
    <t s="4">(wonders)</t>
    <t s="5">—the third-person language refers to Moshe,</t>
    <t s="6">for the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt was through Moshe.</t>
    <t s="7">And according to the above, that in the redemption of the Exodus the channel was also opened for the future redemption,</t>
    <t s="8">it follows</t>
    <t s="9">that Moshe opened the channel for the wonders that will be in the future redemption.</t>
    <t s="10">However, even so, this was with him in concealment.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is the meaning of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="12">that in the future, the wonders that he opened in the Exodus from Egypt will be revealed to him.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="22">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Alternatively, the third-person "I will show him" instructs each Jew that to see future wonders, one must reveal the aspect of Moshe within, combining self-nullification of revelation with acceptance of the yoke.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Also, it can be said</t>
    <t s="1">that this "I will show him"</t>
    <t s="2">(wonders)</t>
    <t s="3">—the third-person language refers to Moshe,</t>
    <t s="4">is an instruction to every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="5">that in order to merit seeing the wonders of the future, it is through the revelation of the aspect of Moshe within him.</t>
    <t s="6">For although the self-nullification of Moshe is a self-nullification of absolute non-existence, nevertheless, the drawing down of the matter of "I will show him wonders" is through the self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke</t>
    <t s="7">(as explained in section 9),</t>
    <t s="8">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="9">in order for the drawing down to be in revelation</t>
    <t s="10">("I will show him")</t>
    <t s="11">there must also be the self-nullification that stems from revelations</t>
    <t s="12">(through contemplation that everything before Him is considered as nothing,</t>
    <t s="13">and the like),</t>
    <t s="14">and through this there will be "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="15">that the wonders of the future will be in revelation,</t>
    <t s="16">with the coming of Mashiach our righteous one, speedily and truly.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
